problems.title: Reflection in the y-axis
problems.question: Reflect A=(4,9) in the y-axis.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)$.
steps: Change only the sign of the x coordinate to obtain (−4,9).

problems.title: Point symmetry about the origin
problems.question: Reflect (−6,7) in the origin and find the coordinate sum.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$.
steps: The reflected point is (6,−7). Its coordinate sum is −1.

problems.title: Number of terms in a geometric polynomial
problems.question: How many monomials remain after canceling (x⁹−1)/(x−1)?
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
steps: The polynomial contains one term for each power from 0 through 8, giving 9 terms. The original rational expression still excludes x=1.

problems.title: Distance to a tangent and parallel diameter
problems.question: A point on a circle is 3 cm from a tangent and 5 cm from the largest chord parallel to it. Find diameter.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: The largest chord is a diameter; the parallel tangent is one radius R from it.
steps: The point is 5 from the central diameter, so R≥5. If the point were on the other side from the tangent, its tangent distance would be R+5, which cannot be 3.
It is on the tangent side, so R−5=3 and R=8. Diameter=16.

problems.title: When circles meet
problems.question: Radii are 11 and 3. Which listed centre distance 7,8,9,11,12,14 cannot give a common point?
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Intersecting or tangent circles require $|R-r|\le d\le R+r$.
steps: The permitted interval is [8,14]. Only 7 lies outside it.

problems.title: Cancel a common factor in a power fraction
problems.question: Calculate (14·2⁶−7·2³)/(5·7·8).
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Factor the numerator before dividing.
steps: The numerator is 7×8×(2×8−1)=7×8×15. Cancel 7×8 and divide 15 by 5, giving 3.

problems.title: A linear system
problems.question: Solve 2x−3y=−5,4x+2y=14 and find x+y.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Eliminate one variable by adding suitable multiples.
steps: Double the first equation: 4x−6y=−10. Subtract it from the second: 8y=24, so y=3.
Then 2x−9=−5 gives x=2, hence x+y=5.

problems.title: Factor a quartic into two quadratics
problems.question: Factor a⁴+4 into two polynomials of positive degree.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Add and subtract $4a^2$, then use a difference of squares.

problems.title: The hypotenuse and two circle radii
problems.question: A right triangle has legs 5,12. Find hypotenuse; its circumradius minus inradius is 4.5.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
steps: c=√169=13. Then R=6.5,r=2 and R−r=4.5, agreeing with the extra information.

problems.title: Three tangent circles in a sixty-degree angle
problems.question: Three distinct circles touch both sides of a 60° angle; the first touches the second externally, and the second touches the third externally. The smallest radius is 3. Find distance between smallest and largest centres.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: A centre is $r/\sin30°=2r$ from the vertex; external tangency gives $2(R-r)=R+r$.
steps: The centres lie along the angle bisector, and consecutive tangent radii satisfy R=3r. Three distinct linked radii must therefore be 3,9,27.
Their centre distances from the vertex are 6,18,54. The extreme-centre distance is 54−6=48.

problems.title: Parallel linear functions
problems.question: y=kx+b goes through (2,3) and is parallel to y=3x+7. Find k+b.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
steps: k=3; 3=3×2+b gives b=−3. Therefore k+b=0.

problems.title: Perpendicular linear functions
problems.question: y=kx+b goes through (4,7) and is perpendicular to y=4x+5. Find kb.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Perpendicular slopes satisfy $4k=-1$.
steps: k=−1/4. Substitute the point: 7=−1+b, giving b=8. Thus kb=−2.

problems.title: Reflect then translate
problems.question: A=(2,−3) translates to (−3,2). Apply the same translation to the reflection of C=(−5,1) in the x-axis.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Reflection: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$; translation vector = destination minus starting point.
steps: The vector is (−5,5). The reflection of C is (−5,−1), so its image is (−10,4).

problems.title: A circumcentre and an equilateral auxiliary triangle
problems.question: B=60°,C=40°. M∈AB,N∈BC,K∈AC satisfy MN=BN,KN=KC. O is circumcentre of KNC. Find ONM.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Isosceles base angles are equal; a central angle is twice an inscribed angle on the same minor arc.
steps: Triangle BMN has BN=MN and angle B=60°, so it is equilateral; angle MNC=120°.
In KNC, equal sides KN=KC give both base angles 40° and apex K=100°. Its circumcentre lies below line NC. The minor central angle NOC is 160°, so ONC=(180°−160°)/2=10° on that lower side.
Ray NM is above NC, so ONM=120°+10°=130°.

problems.title: Transfer an angle between two intersecting circles
problems.question: Two circles meet at A,B. Chord CA of the first is extended past A to K on the second; DB is extended past B to E on the second. AKE=α. Find ACD.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°; opposite rays make supplementary angles.
steps: In cyclic quadrilateral AKEB, ABE=180°−α. Since BD is opposite BE, ABD=α.
In cyclic quadrilateral CABD, ACD+ABD=180°. Therefore ACD=180°−α.

problems.title: Divisibility of a power sum for six indices
problems.question: For how many integers n∈[1,6] is 2ⁿ+2^(n+1)+2^(n+3) divisible by 22?
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
steps: Every n≥1 supplies a factor 2, making the product divisible by 22. All six integers work.

problems.title: A sum of squares equal to zero
problems.question: x²−2xy+2y²+4y+4=0. Find x+y for real x,y.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: The expression is $(x-y)^2+(y+2)^2$.
steps: Both squares must vanish. Thus y=−2 and x=y=−2, giving x+y=−4.

problems.title: Sum powers of two
problems.question: Calculate 2+2²+…+2¹².
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
steps: Remove the initial 1 to obtain 2¹³−2=8190.

problems.title: Altitude extensions meet the circumcircle
problems.question: Altitudes from A,B,C meet the circumcircle again at M,N,K respectively. A=40°,B=C=70°. Find KMN.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: An inscribed angle equals half the arc it intercepts.
steps: At B, the altitude BN makes 90°−C=20° with BC, so minor arc CN=40°. Similarly arc BK=40°. Arc BC through M is 2A=80°.
Thus the arc KBCN containing M totals 40°+80°+40°=160°. The opposite arc KN has measure 360°−160°=200°.
Angle KMN intercepts that opposite arc and equals 200°/2=100°.

problems.title: Two perpendicular feet lie on a circle
problems.question: P lies inside acute angle ABC; PM⊥AB,PN⊥BC. If MBP=30°, find MNP.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Right angles BMP and BNP put B,M,P,N on the circle with diameter BP.
steps: Angles MBP and MNP subtend the same chord MP, from the same side. They are equal, so MNP=30°.

problems.title: Substitute a linear function into an equation
problems.question: Solve f(x−2)+3f(x+1)=16 if f(t)=4t−1.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Use the input t exactly where it appears.
steps: f(x−2)=4x−9 and f(x+1)=4x+3. Their weighted sum is 4x−9+12x+9=16x. Thus 16x=16 and x=1.

problems.title: Factor a common sum
problems.question: Evaluate a²b−ab+a²c−ac for a=3,b+c=4.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Factor as $a(a-1)(b+c)$.
steps: Substitution gives 3×2×4=24.

problems.title: Exactly one intersection with a piecewise graph
problems.question: y=3x−2 intersects the graph given by y=5x−22 for x>a and y=−3x−20 for x<1 exactly once. Which listed a works?
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Solve against each branch and retain its input restriction.
steps: The lower branch meets the line at x=−3, valid because −3<1. The upper meets it at x=10, valid only if 10>a.
Exactly one intersection requires a≥10. Among the choices 3,9,1,10,5,4, only 10 works.
problems.answer: a=10 among the choices; all a≥10 give one intersection.

problems.title: A circumradius-chord angle from an altitude
problems.question: O is the circumcentre and BK an altitude. ABK=70°. Find OBC.
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: $BK\perp AC$; radius-chord angle $\angle OBC=|90°-A|$.
steps: The smaller angle between AB and AC is 90°−70°=20°, so A=20° or 160°, according to the altitude-foot configuration.
In either case |90°−A|=70°. This follows also by using isosceles triangle BOC and the inscribed-angle theorem.

problems.title: Two possible inscribed angles from one central angle
problems.question: O is circumcentre, AOC=60°, and I is incenter. Which listed AIC is possible?
problems.idea: Use the stated algebraic or geometric relation and verify that all conditions hold.
formulas: Angle B is half an arc AC not containing B; $\angle AIC=90°+B/2$.
steps: The minor arc AC is 60°. If B is on the major arc, angle B=30°, giving AIC=105°. If B is on the minor arc, B=150°, giving AIC=165°.
Only 105° is listed.
problems.answer: 105° among the choices; the geometry allows 105° or 165°.
